definition: Cobbler means a person who makes or repairs shoes.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cobbler. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cobbler should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A good cobbler can tell you where you walk heavy; Mr. Abara read the mayor's worn heels like a diary.
A patcher is milder than a cobbler on this scale — glue slapped where the sole flaps, the shoe handed back while you wait; the cobbler owns the deeper craft, repairing the shoe to outlast the glue.
A bootmaker goes further than a cobbler — the cobbler restores a boot someone else built; the bootmaker cuts the first piece of hide and builds the whole boot around a customer's foot.

A shoemaker builds new shoes from the first cut of leather; tradition hands the cobbler the other half of the trade — mending what someone else built. The two crafts overlap at the bench, but the split survives: shoemaker for the making, cobbler for the worn heel brought back to life.

A mender is anyone who repairs anything — nets, kettles, fences, hems. Cobbler narrows the field to a single trade: shoes, and only shoes, mended by hand. Every cobbler is a mender the moment a sole crosses the bench; bring a cobbler your torn coat and you are at the wrong counter.

At sixteen, Amara wanted to design sneakers; her grandfather offered her a summer at his bench instead.
He was the last cobbler on the block, and his work began where a factory's ended: boots resoled, heels rebuilt, stitching replaced along seams that machines had given up on.
Nothing new was ever made there.
Everything that crossed the counter was already loved and already worn out.
By August, Amara could strip a ruined heel and rebuild it so the repair outlived the boot's original parts.
She went back to sketching sneakers in the fall -- but now every design she drew could be taken apart and fixed.
